1.meaning: Two of the 'disconnected letters' (al-muqaṭṭaʿāt) — the Arabic letters Ḥā and Mīm recited individually by name rather than read as a word. Several sūrahs open with such isolated letters; their precise meaning is known to Allah, and they serve to call attention and to point to the miraculous nature of a revelation composed from the very letters people use in their own speech.
1.grammar: These are letter-names recited individually, not an inflected word, so they carry no case ending or tense. The long pronunciation (ḥā, mīm) is how the letters are spelled out by name; they stand outside the normal grammar of a sentence.

1.meaning: A sending-down or gradual revelation; the verbal noun for the act of causing something to descend, used especially for scripture sent down from on high stage by stage.
1.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of an action) on the intensive pattern tafʿīl, which carries a sense of doing something repeatedly or in stages. The final -u is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or stands as a heading naming a thing.

2.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
2.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

3.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: One who is mighty, invincible, and unassailable — possessing overwhelming might and dignity that none can overcome; also carries the sense of being precious and held in high honor. As a divine name it points to Allah's irresistible power.
5.grammar: A definite adjective/noun on the intensive paradigm faʿīl, denoting a deeply established quality. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the Mighty') or follows a preposition.
5.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, invincibility, honor

6.meaning: 'The Wise.' An adjective describing one possessing ḥikma — sound, perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right and fitting place. As a divine attribute it denotes flawless wisdom in all decree and command.

parts.en: wise / full of wisdom (in the genitive, '-i')

6.grammar: An adjective in an intensive pattern ('deeply/perfectly wise'). The al- means 'the.' The final -i vowel is the genitive case — the form used after a preposition, or when describing a noun that is itself genitive, or linking in an 'of …' relationship.
6.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to be wise, judge soundly, put things in their right place

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

3.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

4.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
4.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

5.meaning: Surely signs, tokens, or clear indications; evidences that point to a greater truth. The prefixed lām adds emphasis ('surely / indeed').
5.grammar: An emphatic particle 'la-' ('surely') joined to an indefinite feminine plural noun ('signs'). The -āt- is the sound feminine plural marker; the final -in (nunation) marks it indefinite. For this plural pattern the -in form serves for both the accusative and the genitive case.
5.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token

6.meaning: 'For the believers' — for those who have faith: those who trust, affirm, and feel secure in their belief in Allah and what He has revealed.
6.grammar: A masculine sound plural active participle ('believers') with the -īna ending, here the genitive/oblique form required after the preposition li- ('for, to'). With the article, li- + al- contracts to lil-.
6.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust; (form IV) to believe, to have faith

1.meaning: 'And in' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in / within / during.'
1.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the preposition fī ('in'). Fī governs the following noun, putting it into the genitive case. Neither particle changes form.

2.meaning: Your creation — the act or result of creating you; refers to the fashioning of humanity from the earth and the stages of human development.
2.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) from the root kh-l-q (to create), in the genitive case (kasra) as the second term of an iḍāfa (possessive construction), followed by the second-person plural possessive suffix -kum. Meaning: 'the creation of you all' or 'your creation.'
2.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, bring into being

3.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
3.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

4.meaning: He disperses / He scatters — refers to Allah scattering and spreading living creatures throughout the earth.

parts.en: He disperses / He spreads / He scatters

4.grammar: Third-person masculine singular imperfect (present/future) verb from the root b-th-th (to scatter, spread, disperse). The doubled final consonant (shaddah on ث) indicates the intensified form. Subject is Allah (implied from context).

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'a moving/walking creature / a beast / any living thing that treads the earth' — broadly, any animal that moves along the ground.
6.grammar: A singular indefinite feminine noun (originally an active participle, 'one that moves/treads'). The ending -tin combines the feminine marker (tā' marbūṭa) with tanwīn showing indefiniteness and the genitive case — the form typically used after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of …'). The final '-n' sound is spoken but unwritten.
6.root: د-ب-ب (d-b-b) — to move/creep/walk gently along the ground

7.meaning: Signs, tokens, or evidences; also the discrete verses of revelation. Each is a clear indicator pointing to a greater truth or to its divine source.
7.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun. The ending -tun consists of the feminine plural marker -āt together with the nominative case (used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing who/what something is) and nunation (the -n sound) marking it as indefinite ('signs', not 'the signs').

8.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
8.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
8.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

9.meaning: Those who attain firm, sure certainty — people who know without doubt, having reached settled, unwavering conviction (especially in matters of faith).
9.grammar: A present-tense verb on the form-IV ('afʿala') pattern (to be certain/have certitude), third-person masculine plural. The 'yu-' prefix and -ūna ending together mean 'they (males/mixed) do'; the -ūna is the plain indicative form, marking an ordinary present statement of a settled trait.

1.meaning: And the alternation / difference — variation and succession one after another (as with turns of night and day), or divergence and disagreement between things.
1.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' A verbal noun (form VIII 'ikhtilāf') meaning succession/alternation or divergence. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically linking to a following noun ('the alternation OF …') or following a preposition.

2.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
2.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').

3.meaning: And the day / daytime — the period of light from dawn to sunset.
3.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and'; 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'n', said an-nahār). A noun for the daylight hours. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the day').

4.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
4.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
5.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.
5.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — coming down, descending, alighting

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
6.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
6.root: — (proper divine name)

7.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
7.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

8.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
8.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: 'Provision, sustenance' — rizq is whatever Allah bestows that benefits a creature: food, wealth, and every good thing one is granted to live on.
10.grammar: A singular indefinite noun with the -in ending, which is the genitive with tanwīn. The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('some of (the) provision …').
10.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, that which is bestowed to live on

11.meaning: And so He gave life, revived, brought to life what was lifeless; the causative sense 'to make alive'.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb introduced by 'fa' ('and so / then', often signalling a result or sequence). The verb is third-person masculine singular ('he gave life'); the prefixed 'a' belongs to the causative (Form IV) pattern, turning 'to live' into 'to give life'.

12.meaning: By it, with it, through it; the preposition 'bi' (with/by means of) joined to a pronoun referring to something previously mentioned.
12.grammar: A preposition plus an attached third-person masculine singular pronoun ('it / him'). 'Bi' conveys instrument or means ('by means of it'); the pronoun takes the -i vowel because words governed by 'bi' stand in the genitive.

13.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
13.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'

14.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
14.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
14.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

15.meaning: Its death, its lifelessness or dormancy; the state of being dead, joined to a possessor.
15.grammar: A noun ('death') with an attached third-person feminine singular possessive pronoun ('its / her'). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, the case taken before a possessor pronoun and after prepositions ('death of it').

16.meaning: And in the directing / shifting — refers to the alternation and change of winds as a sign of Allah's power.
16.grammar: Conjunction waw (and) followed by the verbal noun taṣrīf from the root ṣ-r-f (to direct, turn, shift), on the intensive pattern tafʿīl indicating repeated or varied action. Genitive case (kasra ending) as part of an iḍāfa. Often rendered 'the variation/direction of the winds.'
16.root: ص-ر-ف (ṣ-r-f) — to direct, turn, divert, vary

17.meaning: The winds, moving currents of air.
17.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the winds'): the definite article 'al-' assimilates to the following sun-letter 'r' (so it is written and pronounced 'ar-r'), attached to the noun stem 'riyāḥ'. The final -i ending is genitive, taken after a preposition or when the noun is possessed by a preceding noun ('… of the winds').

18.meaning: Signs, tokens, or evidences; also the discrete verses of revelation. Each is a clear indicator pointing to a greater truth or to its divine source.
18.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun. The ending -tun consists of the feminine plural marker -āt together with the nominative case (used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing who/what something is) and nunation (the -n sound) marking it as indefinite ('signs', not 'the signs').

19.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
19.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
19.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

20.meaning: They use their reason, they understand and reflect; to grasp things with the intellect and restrain oneself accordingly.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -na ending also signals the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action ('they use reason').
20.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to reason, understand; to restrain (as a tether restrains)

1.meaning: That; a demonstrative used to point to something distant or already mentioned. It singles out a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing, roughly 'that one over there.'
1.grammar: A feminine singular demonstrative pronoun pointing to something far off. The -ka element signals remoteness ('that yonder' rather than 'this near'). Being a demonstrative, it does not take case endings; its form is fixed.

2.meaning: "signs / verses / tokens" — the plural of āya, a 'sign' or evident token that points to something beyond itself; it also denotes a verse of revelation, each one a sign.
2.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks sound feminine plural). The final -u is the nominative case, the form taken as the subject of a sentence or the leading term of a possessive chain ('the signs OF …').

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: "We recite it / We relate it" — built on the verb meaning to recite aloud, to read out, to convey a text in sequence; with the object pronoun it means 'we recite them/it'.
4.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'we' form. The na- prefix marks first-person plural ('we'). The attached -hā is the object 'it/them' (referring to a feminine or non-human-plural noun).
4.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read out, follow

5.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

6.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
6.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
6.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

7.meaning: So in/by which …? — a compound of 'so/then', the preposition 'in/by', and the interrogative 'which/what'. It opens a question asking 'in which?' or 'by what?', expecting a specific item to be identified.
7.grammar: A particle cluster: 'fa-' links to what precedes ('so/then'); 'bi-' is the preposition 'in/by/with'. The interrogative 'ayy' carries the -i ending because it is genitive, the case required after a preposition. It questions which one of a class is meant, and normally precedes a following noun ('which … ?').

8.meaning: Speech, talk, or an account; a piece of discourse or report — that which is newly spoken or related.
8.grammar: An indefinite singular noun ('a talk / a report'). The -in ending is genitive with nunation (the -n marking 'a/an'), the form taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …').
8.root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th) — to be new, to happen; to relate, to speak

9.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
9.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
9.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: 'And His signs / His verses' — the plural of 'sign,' meaning tokens, proofs, or marks that point to a greater reality, and also the verses of revelation. The attached 'His' refers the signs to Allah, and the leading 'and' connects them to what precedes.
11.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun. The -i ending on the plural marks the genitive case, used when a noun is possessed ('… OF …'), follows a preposition, or (as here) carries an attached possessor. The suffix -hi means 'his,' and its vowel is i to harmonize with the preceding genitive. The opening wa- means 'and.'
11.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark, or evidence

12.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
12.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

1.meaning: Woe — an exclamation of severe warning, condemnation, or lamentation; used to express doom and destruction upon someone.
1.grammar: A noun (in the nominative case, marked by tanwīn -un) used as an exclamation of condemnation. It is indeclinable in some usages but here carries the nominative indefinite marker. 'Waylun li-' means 'woe to [someone].'
1.root: و-ي-ل (w-y-l) — destruction, ruin, woe (no productive verb in Classical Arabic)

2.meaning: For every, for each, belonging to all of. Combines the preposition 'for/to' with the word for 'every/all.'
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('for/to') joined to kull ('every/each/all'). The -i ending on kull is genitive, the case required after a preposition. The combination conveys 'for every / to each.'

3.meaning: A great liar / a habitual fabricator — an intensive adjective (faʿʿāl pattern) meaning one who lies excessively and fabricates widely; a shameless deceiver.

parts.en: a great liar / a habitual fabricator (indefinite genitive)

3.grammar: The -in ending (tanwīn kasra) marks indefinite genitive (in a construct chain or after a preposition). affāk is the faʿʿāl intensive form: one who constantly produces falsehood and fabrication.
3.root: أ-ف-ك (ā-f-k) — to lie, to fabricate; turning away from truth

4.meaning: A sinner; one steeped in sin and wrongdoing. An emphatic form denoting someone given over to guilt and transgression.
4.grammar: A masculine adjective/noun on an intensive pattern (faʿīl) ('deeply, habitually sinful'). The final -in (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a sinner') and in the genitive case, the form used after a preceding noun or a preposition.
4.root: أ-ث-م (ʾ-th-m) — to sin, do wrong; guilt

1.meaning: Who hears / he who listens — referring to someone who listens to the signs and revelations of Allah.
1.grammar: Third-person masculine singular imperfect (present) verb from the root s-m-ʿ (to hear, listen). The -u ending is the indicative mood marker. Here it is used in a relative/descriptive sense: 'one who hears.'
1.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, listen, perceive by hearing

2.meaning: Signs, tokens, or evident proofs; also used for the discrete verses of revelation. An āya is a marker that points beyond itself to a deeper truth or to its Author.
2.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs/verses'). The sound-feminine plural takes -i in both the genitive and accusative; the -i ending here links it to a following noun ('… of …') or marks it as the object of a verb or preposition.

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: It is being recited or read aloud — said of verses or scripture conveyed by voice, in an ongoing or repeated manner.

parts.en: recite/read aloud (passive stem, root letters t-l + long ā)

4.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) passive verb in the third person feminine singular ('it/she is recited'). The tu- prefix marks both the present tense and the passive voice ('is being …-ed'), so the doer is unnamed and the focus is on what undergoes the action. The stem -tlā keeps the second root consonant (t) and ends in a long ā written with ى, the shape a weak-final (defective) root takes when no further ending is attached.
4.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

5.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
5.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

6.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
6.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

7.meaning: He persists / he continues stubbornly — referring to one who insists on disbelief or wrongdoing despite having heard the truth.

parts.en: he persists / he insists / he is stubborn

7.grammar: Third-person masculine singular imperfect verb from the root ṣ-r-r (to persist, insist, be stubborn), Form IV (yufiʿilu pattern) or some analyses place it in Form I with doubled root. The doubled rā (shaddah) marks the geminated root. Indicative mood ending -u.
7.root: ص-ر-ر (ṣ-r-r) — to persist, insist, be obstinate

8.meaning: arrogantly / disdainfully
8.grammar: active participle, Form X (اسْتَكْبَرَ), masculine singular, accusative case with tanwīn, functioning as ḥāl (circumstantial descriptor)
8.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great, to be arrogant

9.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'as if / as though.' It introduces a comparison or likeness, treating a situation as resembling another — presenting something as if it were a certain way, whether or not it truly is.
9.grammar: A particle of comparison formed from 'ka-' ('like / as') joined to a particle meaning 'that.' Together they function as a single linking word, 'as if,' used to liken one circumstance to another. It is a particle, so it has no case ending of its own.

10.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
10.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

11.meaning: he hears them

parts.en: them / it (3rd person feminine singular pronoun suffix)

11.grammar: verb, imperfect jussive (مجزوم), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular; with object pronoun هَا (referring to آيات — the verses)

12.meaning: So give him glad tidings / announce good news to him: to convey welcome, joyful news that visibly gladdens. The command is directed at one male addressee and carries an attached 'him' as the one receiving the good news.
12.grammar: A Form II imperative (command) addressed to a second-person masculine singular ('you, give good news'), with attached object pronoun -hu ('him'). The prefix fa- means 'so/then'. The intensive Form II conveys actively delivering joyful news. A command form takes no case vowel; its base ends in a silent stop (sukūn) before the pronoun.
12.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — good news, glad tidings; to gladden

13.meaning: With/of a punishment: 'with' joined to a word for a chastisement, torment, or penalty inflicted as recompense; indefinite ('a punishment').
13.grammar: An indefinite noun with the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('with / of'). The ending -in does two things: the final -n (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a punishment'), and the -i vowel is the genitive case required after the preposition 'bi-'.

14.meaning: Painful / agonizing: causing intense pain; said of something that grieves and torments deeply. An intensive adjective, so 'sorely painful'. Indefinite ('a painful …').
14.grammar: An indefinite adjective on an intensive pattern (conveying 'deeply/sorely painful'). The ending -in shows both indefiniteness (the final -n, nunation: 'a painful one') and the genitive case (the -i vowel), the case that an adjective takes to match a genitive noun it describes or that follows a preposition.

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: 'He knew / came to know / had knowledge of'. The verb denotes knowing with certainty — being aware of and acquainted with a thing's reality.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he …'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for a completed action done by 'he'. It states that the knowing took place and is settled.

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: Our signs / verses. The plural of āya — a sign, token, or miraculous proof, and also a verse of revelation — with the attached 'our'.
4.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs / verses') with the possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). The sound feminine plural ending -āt shows -i, the case used for the genitive (linked to a following word or after a preposition) and the accusative (object of a verb); attaching -nā ('our') also places it in a possessive relationship. So it means 'signs belonging to Us'.

5.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
5.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'
5.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — thing, to will

6.meaning: He takes them / he adopts them — referring to someone who takes Allah's signs or the Quran as a mockery or amusement.

parts.en: he took them / he adopted them (feminine object)

6.grammar: Third-person masculine singular perfect (past) verb from the root ʾ-kh-dh (to take), Form VIII (iftaʿala): ittakhadha, meaning 'to take for oneself, adopt, consider as.' The suffix -hā is the third-person feminine singular object pronoun referring to āyāt (signs, verses, feminine plural treated as feminine singular).
6.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, adopt

7.meaning: Mockery, ridicule, a laughing-stock — the act of deriding, or an object treated as a joke. Huzuw is scornful jesting that belittles.
7.grammar: An indefinite verbal noun in the accusative ('an' written with tanwīn on a final alif). The accusative here is typical for the object of a verb or for stating what something is taken/treated 'as'. 'Indefinite' means 'mockery / a mockery' rather than 'the mockery'.
7.root: ه-ز-و (h-z-w) — to mock, ridicule, scoff at; a wāw-final variant of the related root ه-ز-أ (h-z-ʾ), this written form ending in wāw

8.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
8.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

9.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

10.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
10.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

11.meaning: 'Humiliating / disgracing / degrading' — an active participle describing something that brings abasement and disgrace upon its object.
11.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word, like '-ing' in English) from the causative (form IV) pattern, meaning 'one that causes humiliation.' The -un ending (indefinite nominative tanwīn) marks an indefinite noun in the nominative case — the case of a subject or, commonly, of something described as existing ('a humiliating [thing]').
11.root: ه-و-ن (h-w-n) — being lowly, easy, contemptible; hence humiliation

1.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
1.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

2.meaning: Before them / in front of them — referring to what lies ahead of the disbelievers, typically Hellfire or punishment awaiting them.
2.grammar: Conjunction waw followed by warāʾa (behind, in front of, beyond) — a preposition/adverb — with the third-person masculine plural possessive suffix -him. The word warāʾ can mean both 'behind' and 'before/in front of' depending on context. Here it indicates what awaits them (Hell).
2.root: و-ر-ء (w-r-ʾ) — behind, beyond, in front of

3.meaning: Hell / Jahannam — the proper name of the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter.
3.grammar: A proper name (the name of Hell), treated as a feminine, non-fully-inflecting noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, marking it as the subject/predicate of a statement ('… is Jahannam'). Because it is a proper name of this type, it does not take the usual final '-n' (tanwīn) of ordinary nouns.

4.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
4.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

5.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'it avails, suffices, benefits, or makes free from need' — to be of use against something or to enrich and relieve someone of need. The root centres on richness, sufficiency, and being free of want.
5.grammar: An ongoing or future action. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the form (causative pattern) carries the sense of 'to make sufficient' or 'to be of avail'. The final long -ī is the verb's own weak-root termination.
5.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, sufficient

6.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
6.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.
6.root: — (a preposition; no triliteral verbal root)

7.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
7.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

8.meaning: 'They earned / they acquired / they gained' — past-tense action of a group obtaining something through their own effort, whether good or bad. The root carries the sense of working to acquire, and is often used of the deeds people accrue.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -ū marks a masculine plural subject ('they') who completed the action in the past.

9.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
9.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

10.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
10.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: Past-tense verb (reflexive form), third person plural: 'they took for themselves, adopted, chose.' A completed act of taking something on as one's own.
12.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in a reflexive pattern (taking something for oneself). The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural). The opening 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the cluster of consonants be pronounced.

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
14.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
14.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
16.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

17.meaning: 'And for them / and they have.' A combination expressing possession or entitlement belonging to a group of males: 'and to/for them (belongs).' The particle li- conveys 'for' or 'belonging to,' and the attached pronoun refers to 'them.'
17.grammar: A possessive/benefactive phrase: the preposition li- ('for, belonging to') with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them,' masculine plural). Such 'for X' phrases commonly express that something belongs to or is owed to that party.

18.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
18.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

19.meaning: Great, immense, mighty — vast in magnitude or importance. Describes something tremendous, whether in size, weight, or gravity.
19.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern, conveying a strong, established quality. The '-un' ending marks it nominative and indefinite; as an adjective it typically agrees with and describes an indefinite noun ('a great …').

1.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
1.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

2.meaning: Guidance — right direction, the showing of the correct way and the leading along it. The term combines pointing out the path and granting success in following it; more than mere information, it is direction toward what is right.

parts.en: indefinite (tanwin) ending on a shortened final vowel

2.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun. The -an (tanwin) ending marks indefiniteness — 'a guidance' rather than 'the guidance'. Because the word ends in a weak final letter, its case is not audibly distinguished, so this single form covers more than one grammatical position.

3.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
3.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

4.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

5.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
5.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
5.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

6.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
6.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

7.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
7.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

8.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
8.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

9.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
9.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

10.meaning: Filth / impurity / torment — used to describe a punishment or degrading chastisement; also means moral corruption or an abominable penalty.
10.grammar: A noun in the genitive case (kasra + tanwīn, indefinite), following a preposition. Rijz/rijs refers to something abominable, filthy, or a severe punishment. Here it indicates a painful, debasing torment.

11.meaning: Painful / grievous — describing a torment that is intensely hurtful and severe.
11.grammar: An adjective (ṣifa) in the nominative case with indefinite tanwīn (-un), from the root ʾ-l-m (to be in pain). The pattern faʿīl indicates an intensive or established quality: 'very painful.' It agrees in definiteness and case with the noun it modifies.
11.root: أ-ل-م (ʾ-l-m) — to be in pain, to hurt

1.meaning: Allah — the proper name of the One God, the sole and absolute Deity worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a name, not a common noun, and refers to the Creator and Sustainer of all that exists.
1.grammar: The proper divine name. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject (the doer) of a sentence or the noun being identified.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: To make subservient, to harness or press into service; to bring something under control so it obediently serves a purpose. The Form II verb intensifies the sense of subjugating for use.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in Form II (to make serve). The bare form with final -a marks a completed action by a single masculine 'he' ('he made subservient').
3.root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r) — to subject, harness, press into service

4.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
4.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

5.meaning: 'The sea' — a large body of water; the deep. By extension it can denote any vast expanse of water.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('the sea'). The '-a' ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
5.root: ب-ح-ر (b-ḥ-r) — sea, vast expanse of water

6.meaning: A verb phrase meaning 'so that it may run/flow/sail' or 'in order that it may move along'. It joins the purpose particle 'li-' with the verb for flowing, running, or sailing (as water flows or a ship runs over the sea).
6.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person feminine singular ('it/she'), in the subjunctive after the purpose particle 'li-' ('so that'). The 'ta-' prefix marks a feminine subject. The final '-ya' (here written on the weak letter) is the subjunctive ending forced by 'li-', signalling purpose or intended result ('so that it may flow/sail').
6.root: ج-ر-ي (j-r-y) — to run, to flow, to stream, to sail along

7.meaning: the ships / the vessel(s)
7.grammar: noun, definite, nominative — al-fulk is remarkable in Arabic for being both singular and plural (like English 'sheep'); the -u ending marks the nominative; it can refer to a single ship or to ships collectively; used in Quranic contexts for the ships that sail the seas by Allah's permission

8.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

9.meaning: With/by His command — amr means a command, order, decree, or matter/affair; with the preposition bi- ('with, by') and the pronoun 'His' it conveys 'by His command' or 'by His decree'.
9.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with' or 'by'. The noun amr takes the genitive -i ending (required after the preposition bi-) and then the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by the preposition.
9.root: ء-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, order; a matter/affair

10.meaning: 'And so that you may seek / desire' — to strive after and pursue something, to seek to obtain a benefit or bounty. The Form VIII verb conveys earnest seeking.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb in Form VIII (to seek, desire) with 'and' plus the purpose-particle 'so that'. The ta- prefix means 'you'; the -ū ending (nūn dropped) marks plural 'you all' in the subjunctive of intent ('so that you may seek').
10.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
12.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
12.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

13.meaning: And so that you (plural) may; in the hope that you might. The particle laʿalla expresses hope, expectation, or a desired outcome ('perhaps / so that'), here with 'you' as its subject.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in the hope that

13.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps / in hope that'), which expresses an anticipated or hoped-for result, with the attached pronoun -kum ('you all') as its subject. Such particles place the following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -kum here is that subject. It typically leads into a verb stating the hoped outcome. The wa- ('and') links it to what comes before.

14.meaning: 'You (all) give thanks / are grateful'. To recognize a kindness and acknowledge it — with the heart, tongue, and deeds — toward the one who bestowed it.
14.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix signals a 'you' subject, and the '-ūna' ending marks a plural masculine 'you' in the ongoing (indicative) mood — 'you all give thanks'. The retained '-na' shows the verb stands free of any negating or governing particle.

1.meaning: And He made (something) subservient, harnessed it, or pressed it into service — to bring a thing under control so it works toward an appointed purpose.
1.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The verb is past tense for 'he' (third-person masculine singular); its doubled middle letter marks an intensive/causative pattern ('to make subservient'), and the -a ending is the standard past-tense vowel for a single masculine doer who completed the act.
1.root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r) — to subject, subdue, press into service

2.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

3.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
3.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
5.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

6.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
6.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
6.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

9.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

10.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'from him/it' — indicating origin or source, that something proceeds out of him/it.
10.grammar: The preposition min ('from') with the attached pronoun -hu ('him/it', third-person masculine singular). As the object of a preposition the pronoun stands in the genitive; the combination indicates source or origin.

11.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
11.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
13.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

14.meaning: Surely signs, tokens, or clear indications; evidences that point to a greater truth. The prefixed lām adds emphasis ('surely / indeed').
14.grammar: An emphatic particle 'la-' ('surely') joined to an indefinite feminine plural noun ('signs'). The -āt- is the sound feminine plural marker; the final -in (nunation) marks it indefinite. For this plural pattern the -in form serves for both the accusative and the genitive case.

15.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
15.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
15.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

16.meaning: 'They reflect / ponder / think deeply / contemplate' — a verb for sustained, careful mental consideration and turning a matter over in the mind.
16.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb in an intensive/reflexive pattern conveying deliberate, repeated reflection. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the -ūna ending indicates the indicative mood (a plain factual statement).

1.meaning: An imperative command meaning 'Say!' or 'Speak!' — a direct order to one person to utter or declare something.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male. The bare, vowelless ending (the silent stop on the final 'l') marks it as a direct order: 'you, say!' It is built from the verb 'to say' with the weak middle letter dropped, leaving the short, clipped command form.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

2.meaning: 'For/to those who …' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the masculine plural relative pronoun 'those who,' which introduces a description of a group by something they do.
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to') fused with the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). Relative pronouns like this do not change for case; they point ahead to a clause that describes the group ('those who …').

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: To forgive / that He may forgive — referring to Allah's forgiveness of the believers' sins.

parts.en: they forgive / (that) they may forgive (jussive plural)

4.grammar: Third-person masculine plural imperfect verb from the root gh-f-r (to forgive, cover, pardon). The form yaghfirū is the jussive/subjunctive mood (short vowel ending dropped, waw retained for plural) used after lam of purpose or in a conditional context. However in context this may be 'that Allah may forgive' — the subject varies by reading.

5.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
5.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

6.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
6.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

7.meaning: They hold out hope for something, expecting and longing for a good outcome (often divine reward or mercy). The verb can carry both hoping for good and, in some contexts, fearing/anticipating.
7.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -ūna ending is the indicative form, signalling a real, ongoing or habitual action ('they hope / they keep hoping').

8.meaning: The days — referring to specific days of divine reckoning, or to the historical days of punishment that struck previous nations.
8.grammar: Broken plural (jamʿ taksīr) of yawm (day), in the accusative case (fatḥa ending) as the object of the preposition or as a ẓarf (adverbial of time). Pattern: faʿʿāl → ayyām.

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: '...so that He may reward/requite' — to give due recompense, repaying a person according to their deeds, whether good or ill.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he requites'), preceded by 'li-' meaning 'so that / in order that', which expresses purpose. Because of this particle the verb takes the subjunctive mood, shown by the final '-a' (here '-ya' on the weak-ending verb) instead of the usual '-u' — marking an intended or hoped-for outcome rather than a plain fact. It typically takes an object: the one being recompensed.

11.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
11.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
11.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

12.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
12.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

13.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
13.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

14.meaning: They earn / acquire — to gain, accumulate, or bring upon oneself something through one's own effort or action, whether wealth, deeds, or their consequences (good or bad).
14.grammar: Present-tense verb. The 'ya-' prefix together with the '-ūna' ending marks 'they' (masculine plural) doing the action now or habitually. The full '-ūna' (rather than shortened '-ū') signals the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact, not a command or subjunctive.

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: 'He did / worked / acted' — to perform a deed or action, to do work.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base form. With no added subject-suffix and the final -a, it carries the default third-person masculine singular subject, 'he did'. The past tense presents the action as completed.

3.meaning: "Righteous / good / sound" — an active participle describing one who or that which is upright and wholesome and acts rightly; as a description of deeds it means good, virtuous works.
3.grammar: An active participle used as a noun or adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a righteous one / a good deed') and in the accusative case — the form used for a direct object or other complement.
3.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound / upright / righteous

4.meaning: 'Then it is for his own self/soul' — introducing a consequence that the benefit accrues to a person's own self. The nafs is the inner self, soul, or person — the seat of one's individual being.
4.grammar: fa means 'then/so' (a connective showing result). li- is the preposition 'for/to (the benefit of)', which puts the following noun in the genitive. The -i ending is genitive (required after li-). The suffix -hi is the attached possessive pronoun 'his'.

5.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
5.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
5.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: Does evil / commits harm / acts badly — the act of doing something wrong, wicked, or harmful; to cause ill or injury.

parts.en: he did evil / he acted badly (Form IV perfect verb)

6.grammar: Asāa is a perfect (past) verb in Form IV (afʿala pattern), 3rd person masculine singular. The Form IV prefix a- (realized here in the hamza) makes the root meaning causative/intensive — 'to make bad, to do badly, to commit evil'. The verb has no overt suffix, which marks 3rd person masculine singular in the perfect. In conditional or general-truth contexts it can translate as a present ('does evil') or habitual.
6.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, to be ugly, to cause harm

7.meaning: Then upon it / then it is against her — indicating the consequence falls on the one who acted (against her own soul).

parts.en: then upon it/her — the consequence is on her

7.grammar: Particle fa (then/so) + preposition ʿalā (upon/on) + third-person feminine singular pronoun -hā. The pronoun refers to the nafs (soul, feminine) mentioned earlier. 'Then upon it' means the consequence of one's action falls on one's own soul.

8.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
8.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
9.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

10.meaning: 'Your Lord' — Rabb denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, possesses, and brings each thing to its completion; joined to 'your' (plural).
10.grammar: A noun 'Lord' in the genitive case (the -i ending), which typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The suffix -kum is the possessive 'your' addressed to a group.
10.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship: nurturing, mastering, owning, sustaining

11.meaning: 'You are returned / brought back' — a passive verb from the root meaning to return: the subjects are made to go back, sent back to a point of origin, the action being done to them rather than by them.
11.grammar: Present/future passive. The tu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and the internal vowelling (u–a) makes it passive — the action is done TO the subject. The -ūna ending is the full ('indicative') plural form, used when the verb is not cut short by certain particles.

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: 'We gave / granted / brought'. To hand over or bestow something upon someone; to come to someone with a gift or grant.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative (form IV) sense 'to bring/grant to someone'. The '-nā' suffix is the doer 'we' in completed past time. It often takes two objects — the recipient and the thing given.
2.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to give, bring

3.meaning: Sons of / children of — the plural 'sons' used in a possessive construction meaning 'the descendants or people of' someone.
3.grammar: This is the plural of 'son' in the construct (possessive) state, so it leans on a following name meaning 'the children OF …'. The -ī ending here reflects the construct form (the normal final nūn of the plural drops off when the word is joined to what follows), and it carries an oblique (accusative/genitive) sense rather than a nominative one.

4.meaning: 'Israel' — the proper name Israel, the by-name of the prophet Jacob (Yaʿqūb), and by extension his descendants.
4.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is grammatically 'diptote' (it does not take nunation), so it shows a single '-a' ending in places where ordinary nouns would take genitive '-i'; the '-a' here simply marks its case without the usual variation.

5.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
5.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

6.meaning: And sound judgment, wise discernment, and the authority to decide rightly between matters. The noun denotes wisdom in the sense of correct judgment, governance, and ruling — the ability to put things in their proper place.
6.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'; the al- prefix means 'the'. The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a noun governed in that case.
6.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide wisely, rule

7.meaning: And prophethood — the office and dignity of being a prophet, one chosen by Allah to receive revelation and convey His message. The noun names this divinely bestowed mission and rank.
7.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'; the al- prefix means 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', shown by the doubling). The word ends in tā marbūṭa (ة), the feminine noun ending, which itself carries the case vowel; here it bears the accusative -a, so it is pronounced -ta. The accusative typically marks the word as the object of a verb or a noun governed in that case.
7.root: ن-ب-ء (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; whence 'prophet' as bearer of news from Allah

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'We provided/supplied (them)' — to grant sustenance and provision (food, wealth, blessings, anything one is given to live on). The prefix adds 'and'; the suffix means 'them'.
8.grammar: Past-tense verb. The wa- prefix means 'and'. The -nā ending marks the subject 'we' (completed action), and -hum is the direct object 'them' (a group, masculine/mixed).
8.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, what one is granted to live on

9.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
9.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

10.meaning: 'The good/wholesome things' — that which is pure, pleasant, and lawful, especially good and agreeable food.
10.grammar: A descriptive noun ('good, wholesome') made definite by al- ('the') and put in the feminine sound plural. The -āti ending is the feminine plural in the object or genitive state (its counterpart -ātu is the subject form). It names things characterized as pure and good.
10.root: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b) — to be good, pure, wholesome, pleasant
