11.meaning: A verb meaning 'We favored/preferred (them)' or 'We gave them excellence over others' — to bestow a surplus of merit, advantage, or grace that raises one above others. Built on an intensive pattern. The prefix adds 'and'; the suffix means 'them'.
11.grammar: Past-tense verb on the intensive (fa''ala) pattern ('to give a clear preference/advantage'). The wa- prefix means 'and'. The -nā ending marks the subject 'we' (completed action), and -hum is the direct object 'them' (a group).

12.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
12.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
12.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

13.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
13.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
13.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'and we gave/granted them' — the action of bestowing or conferring something upon a group, with the doer being a plural 'we' and the recipients a plural 'them'. The verb carries the sense of granting or handing over a possession.
1.grammar: The stem is a completed (past) action of giving. The -nā ending attached to the verb marks the doer as 'we' (a plural subject). The final -hum is an attached object pronoun meaning 'them' (third-person masculine plural). The opening wa- is a connective particle meaning 'and'.
1.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come / to bring; in this derived (Form IV) shape, to bring to someone, i.e. to give or grant

2.meaning: Clear, manifest, self-evident — the feminine plural of 'bayyin', describing things that are plainly evident and make matters distinct; an intensive adjective implying something that clarifies and is itself unmistakable.
2.grammar: A sound feminine plural adjective. The '-in' (nunation) ending marks it indefinite and in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case, so it agrees with an indefinite feminine plural noun it describes ('clear ___').
2.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct, evident; to make plain

3.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
3.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

4.meaning: The matter, affair, command, or decision — either a thing being dealt with or an authoritative order that is issued. The definite article marks it as a specific, known matter.
4.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links it to a preceding noun ('… of the matter') or follows a preposition.
4.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; a matter or affair

5.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
5.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'they differed / disagreed / fell into dispute', also 'they varied, became diverse'. The Form VIII root expresses people taking divergent positions or one thing succeeding and differing from another.
6.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb (Form VIII), third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention, not pronounced.
6.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, succeed, differ, be at variance

7.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
7.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
9.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
9.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

10.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

11.meaning: It came to them / he came to them: a completed act of arriving or coming, with the recipients ('them') built into the word.

parts.en: final vowel of the past-tense base (he/it)

11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it … '), expressing a completed action. In this form the 'he/it' subject carries no added suffix — the -a is simply the final vowel resting on the last root letter of the base, not a person marker. The attached -hum(u) is the object pronoun 'them'; its vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before a following word.

12.meaning: Knowledge: sure, certain knowing — grasping a thing as it truly is. As a verbal noun it names the state or body of knowledge itself.
12.grammar: A definite noun with the prefixed article 'al-' ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being named.

13.meaning: A noun in the accusative meaning 'out of envy / resentment / wrongful insolence' — overstepping due bounds, often from jealousy of what others have been given. It commonly functions adverbially to give the motive 'because of envy.'
13.grammar: The -an ending (indefinite accusative, called tanwīn) often marks a word as the reason or manner of an action — answering 'why?' or 'how?' Here it conveys 'out of / because of' the named quality.
13.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — exceeding proper limits; envy, insolence, wrongful desire

14.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
14.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
14.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

15.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
15.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

16.meaning: 'Your Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Owner, the One who nurtures and brings to completion) combined with 'your'. 'Rabb' carries the linked senses of ownership, authority, and ongoing care that raises a thing to its perfection.
16.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive. The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the word as a direct object or governed element. The attached -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
16.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing care, ownership and mastery

17.meaning: he decides / decrees / judges — a verb covering the settling of a matter: to pass judgement, to decree definitively, to bring something to completion or fulfilment.
17.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The verb is from a root whose final letter is weak, so the indicative shows up as a long final -ī. It denotes an ongoing or future act: 'he decides / will judge'.
17.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decree, judge, settle a matter, complete

18.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
18.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
18.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

19.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
19.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
19.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

20.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
20.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

21.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
21.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

22.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
22.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
22.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

23.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
23.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

24.meaning: A verb meaning 'they differ, disagree, or diverge from one another' — to hold conflicting views or take opposing courses; from a root tied to variance and succession.
24.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb in Form VIII (iftaʿala), which often carries a reflexive/reciprocal sense — here mutual differing. The prefix 'ya-' with the ending '-ūna' marks 'they' (masculine plural); the retained -na shows the indicative mood (an ongoing or factual action).
24.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, to differ, succession and divergence

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: We made you / We appointed you / We rendered you (such-and-such). From a root meaning to make, set, place, or designate; with an attached 'you,' it conveys 'We caused you to be' or 'We assigned you.'
2.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we'; the further suffix -ka is the object 'you (one male).' Past tense presents the making/appointing as already done.
2.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, set, place, render, appoint

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

4.meaning: An ordained way / a divinely prescribed path — the sharīʿa is the sacred law and comprehensive way of life given by Allah to a community through a prophet.

parts.en: an ordained way / a divine law / a path to water (accusative indefinite)

4.grammar: A noun in the accusative case (fatḥa + tanwīn) from the root sh-r-ʿ (to prescribe, to legislate; also the path leading to water). The pattern faʿīla denotes something established or made clear. Here it means the divinely ordained path and law given to a community.
4.root: ش-ر-ع (sh-r-ʿ) — to prescribe, to open a path, to legislate

5.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
5.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

6.meaning: The matter, affair, command, or decision — either a thing being dealt with or an authoritative order that is issued. The definite article marks it as a specific, known matter.
6.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links it to a preceding noun ('… of the matter') or follows a preposition.
6.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; a matter or affair

7.meaning: So follow it — a divine command to the Prophet and believers to follow the prescribed path (sharīʿa) given by Allah.
7.grammar: Conjunction fa (so/therefore) + second-person masculine singular imperative of Form VIII ittabaʿa (to follow, to adhere to), from the root t-b-ʿ (to follow). The suffix -hā is the third-person feminine singular object pronoun, referring to sharīʿa.
7.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, to adhere to, to pursue

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: '(You) follow / pursue / take as a path' — a verb meaning to walk after, conform to, and adopt something as one's way, in a form that intensively conveys 'to keep following'.
9.grammar: A present/jussive verb in the reflexive-intensive pattern (iftaʿala). The ta- prefix marks the second-person 'you (one male)'. The silent (vowelless) final consonant is the jussive mood, the form used after negative or conditional particles such as 'do not …' or 'if …'.
9.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

10.meaning: Whims and cravings — inclinations, desires, or passions, especially the kind that pull a person toward what they merely want rather than what is true or right. This is the plural, 'desires'.
10.grammar: A broken (internal) plural of the noun hawā, formed on the pattern afʿāl. The final -a marks the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb. (As a 'diptote', this kind of plural normally takes a plain -a without nunation even when indefinite.) The word denotes the pull of personal desire, often inclining away from truth.
10.root: ه-و-ي (h-w-y) — inclining, falling, the leaning of desire toward something

11.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
11.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

12.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

13.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
13.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

1.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
1.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

2.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
2.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

3.meaning: Will avail / will benefit — used negatively: their knowledge or excuses will not benefit them or save them from punishment.

parts.en: they avail / they benefit / they suffice (subjunctive/jussive plural)

3.grammar: Third-person masculine plural imperfect verb from the root gh-n-y (to be self-sufficient, to avail, to benefit), Form IV (aghnā): yughnī → yughnū (plural with dropped yāʾ in subjunctive/jussive). Often used in negative context: 'will not avail them at all.'
3.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be sufficient, to avail, to benefit

4.meaning: With you / about you / from you — the preposition ʿan ('away from, about, concerning') joined to 'you' (one male); after a verb of being pleased it carries the sense 'pleased WITH you'.
4.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. ʿan basically means moving away from, or 'about/concerning' a topic; paired with a verb of contentment it yields 'pleased with'. The suffix -ka is the second-person masculine singular object ('you', one male). Together: 'with you / concerning you'.

5.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
5.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
7.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

8.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
8.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

9.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
9.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

10.meaning: 'Some of them' / 'a part of them' — a noun meaning 'a portion, part, or some' joined to an attached pronoun 'them'. Often paired with itself to express 'one another / each other'.
10.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the nominative case (the -u ending), which typically marks it as the subject or doer. The suffix -hum is a genitive (possessive) pronoun meaning 'their' (masculine plural); attached to a noun this way it sits in the possessor slot, giving 'some of them'.
10.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

11.meaning: Protectors, close allies, guardians, intimate friends — those bound to one another in loyalty, support, and mutual responsibility. A 'walī' is one who is near and takes charge of another's affairs; the plural gathers many such allies.
11.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of walī. The final -u is the nominative ending, the state a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified (as in 'they are allies').

12.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
12.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
12.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

13.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
13.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
13.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

14.meaning: A protector, guardian, ally, and intimate helper; one who is close and takes charge of another's affairs, supporting and safeguarding them.
14.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that is being described ("… is the protector"). The pattern denotes one who possesses the quality intensely.
14.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, alliance, guardianship, taking charge of another

15.meaning: The God-conscious / the mindful — those who guard themselves against wrongdoing out of reverent awareness of Allah (taqwā), shielding their souls by dutiful caution. The "al-" makes it definite ("the mindful ones").

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

15.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural (singular "muttaqin"). The "-īna" ending is the plural form in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case — used for governed nouns, objects, or after prepositions.

1.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
1.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

2.meaning: Enlightenment / clear insights — the Quran or this revelation is described as baṣāʾir (illuminations), plural of baṣīra, meaning clear proofs that open the eyes of understanding.
2.grammar: Broken plural (jamʿ taksīr) of baṣīra (insight, enlightenment, clear evidence), in the nominative case (-u ending). From the root b-ṣ-r (to see, perceive). The plural baṣāʾir refers to illuminating proofs and evidences that grant spiritual sight.

3.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
3.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

4.meaning: A connective 'and' plus 'guidance' — 'and guidance': right direction, the showing of the correct way, that which leads one rightly.
4.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'hudā' is a noun meaning 'guidance'; because it ends in a special shortened alif, its indefinite ending appears as -an (written with tanwīn over the preceding letter). This -an is the indefinite marker; on such alif-ending nouns the case is not separately shown, so the word can stand as subject, object, or predicate alike.

5.meaning: And mercy — compassion, tenderness, and active kindness shown to others; clemency that issues in relief and care.
5.grammar: An indefinite feminine singular noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a mercy') and in the nominative case, the form used for a subject or for something simply being named. The wa- prefix is 'and.'
5.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

6.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
6.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

7.meaning: Those who attain firm, sure certainty — people who know without doubt, having reached settled, unwavering conviction (especially in matters of faith).
7.grammar: A present-tense verb on the form-IV ('afʿala') pattern (to be certain/have certitude), third-person masculine plural. The 'yu-' prefix and -ūna ending together mean 'they (males/mixed) do'; the -ūna is the plain indicative form, marking an ordinary present statement of a settled trait.

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

2.meaning: Think / suppose — the disbelievers wrongly suppose or assume something about Allah's judgment or about the fate of the righteous and wicked.

parts.en: he thought / he supposed / he reckoned

2.grammar: Third-person masculine singular perfect (past) verb from the root ḥ-s-b (to think, suppose, reckon, account). Pattern faʿila. Used to describe faulty or incorrect assumptions.
2.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to think, suppose, reckon, count

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: They commit / they earn — referring to those who commit evil deeds and sins, wrongly expecting to escape judgment.

parts.en: they committed / they earned (by their own hands)

4.grammar: Third-person masculine plural perfect verb from the root j-r-ḥ (to wound, to earn/gain), Form VIII (iftaʿala): ijtaraḥa, meaning 'to earn/acquire (especially evil deeds) through one's own effort or hand.' The Form VIII adds a reflexive/intensive sense.
4.root: ج-ر-ح (j-r-ḥ) — to wound; to earn, acquire (especially wrongdoing)

5.meaning: 'The evil deeds / bad actions' — plural of sayyi'a, a wrong or evil act, a misdeed or sin; the opposite of a good deed.
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the misdeeds'). The -i ending here is the case marker for the sound feminine plural in the genitive/accusative state, typically signalling that it follows a preposition, links to a preceding noun, or stands as an object.
5.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad/evil; misdeed, wrong

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
6.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
6.root: — (particle; no root)

7.meaning: We will make them / We shall render them — Allah declaring that He will equate or make the righteous and wicked equal, which the disbelievers wrongly assumed.

parts.en: We make them / We render them (subjunctive)

7.grammar: First-person plural imperfect verb of jaʿala (to make, render, place) from the root j-ʿ-l, in the subjunctive mood (fatḥa ending after أَن an). Suffix -hum is the third-person masculine plural object pronoun. 'We make them [equal to...]'
7.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, place, consider as

8.meaning: Like those who — a comparison particle joined to a relative pronoun, meaning 'similar to the ones who…' and pointing to a group defined by what follows.
8.grammar: A compound of the preposition ka- ('like, as'), expressing resemblance, and the masculine plural relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). The relative pronoun is fixed in form and introduces a description; it does not change for case.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
9.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

10.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
10.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

11.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
11.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
11.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

12.meaning: 'Equal / the same / alike' — a noun-adjective expressing equality or sameness; that two or more things stand on a par, with no difference between them. It can also mean a level or even thing.
12.grammar: A noun/adjective. The ending -an is accusative with nunation: the -n sound marks it as indefinite, and the accusative case commonly marks it as a predicate or the thing described/acted upon. The accusative -an is here written with a supporting alif (ـاء).
12.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — being level, equal, even, in balance

13.meaning: Their life / their living — referring to the lifetime and manner of living of the people being addressed or discussed.

parts.en: their life / their living (noun of place/time with possessive)

13.grammar: Noun maḥyā (life, place/time of living) from the root ḥ-y-y/ḥ-y-w (to live), on the pattern mafʿal, with the third-person masculine plural possessive suffix -hum. Accusative or genitive depending on syntactic position.
13.root: ح-ي-ي/و (ḥ-y-y) — to live, to be alive

14.meaning: And their death — paired with 'their life,' indicating that both life and death of people are governed by and recorded with Allah.

parts.en: their death / their dying (nominative with possessive)

14.grammar: Conjunction waw + noun mamāt (death, time/manner of dying) from the root m-w-t (to die), on the pattern mafʿal/mafāl, nominative case (-u ending), with third-person masculine plural possessive suffix -hum.

15.meaning: 'It was evil / how evil it is' — a past-tense verb of blame expressing that something is bad, wretched, or wicked. As a verb of dispraise it conveys strong condemnation of a thing.
15.grammar: A Form I past-tense (perfect) verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final -a is not a separate grammatical ending: it is the third root letter (the hamza, ء) carrying its default fatḥa in the 3rd-person masculine singular perfect. As a frozen verb of blame it functions much like 'how evil is …!'
15.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil, to grieve or distress

16.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
16.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

17.meaning: They judge / they rule — referring to people who set themselves up as judges, or to those who follow their own desires in judgment rather than Allah's law.

parts.en: they judge / they rule / they govern (indicative plural)

17.grammar: Third-person masculine plural imperfect indicative verb from the root ḥ-k-m (to judge, rule, govern). The -ūna ending marks the indicative mood, masculine plural. Form I verb.
17.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, rule, govern, be wise

1.meaning: 'And He created' — a past-tense statement that the act of originating was performed by a single masculine agent (He).
1.grammar: wa is 'and'. khalaqa is a past-tense verb; the final -a marks third-person masculine singular ('he created').

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

4.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, or the planet earth; the world we stand upon, often paired with the heavens to mean all of creation.
4.grammar: A feminine noun, prefixed with 'and' and 'the.' The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a noun governed by certain particles.

5.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
5.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
5.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

6.meaning: And that it may be recompensed / and so that every soul is recompensed — indicating that recording of deeds is for the purpose of just retribution on the Day of Judgment.

parts.en: so that it/they may be recompensed (purpose clause, passive)

6.grammar: Conjunction waw + preposition li (for/so that, expressing purpose) + third-person feminine singular imperfect verb in the subjunctive, passive voice, from the root j-z-y (to recompense, reward, requite). The passive form tuj'zā means 'so that [the soul] may be recompensed.'
6.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to recompense, reward, requite, suffice

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'all, every, each, the whole of.' It expresses totality — when joined to a following noun it means 'every (one)' or 'the entirety of' that thing.
7.grammar: A noun of totality with the final -u ending (nominative). The -u typically marks it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It normally attaches to a following noun to mean 'every / all of' it.

8.meaning: A noun meaning 'soul, self, person, living being.' It denotes the inner self or the whole individual — the seat of life and identity, and by extension a 'person' as a single unit.
8.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a soul'). This form appears after prepositions or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun (such as 'every soul').
8.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being

9.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
9.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

10.meaning: 'It earned / acquired, gained' — said of deeds and their consequences; the root means to gain or acquire something, especially the moral 'earnings' of one's actions.
10.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it.' The past tense presents the action as completed.
10.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

11.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
11.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

12.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

13.meaning: They are wronged / treated unjustly — to suffer ẓulm, the placing of something out of its right place: injustice, oppression, being deprived of one's due. The passive form names being on the receiving end of wrongdoing.
13.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine plural. The yu- prefix (with the internal vowelling) marks the third person and the passive 'are being …', and the -ūna ending makes it 'they' (masculine plural) as the ones undergoing the action: 'they are wronged'. The -na is the indicative marker.

1.meaning: 'Have you then seen / considered?' — a pointed question drawing the single listener's attention: 'Tell me — have you observed?'
1.grammar: A past-tense verb fronted by the question marker a- ('have…?') and fa- ('then'). The -ta ending marks the doer as 'you' (a single male). The phrase invites the listener to reflect on something.

2.meaning: Who / whoever / the one who. A relative and conditional pronoun used for people, introducing a clause that describes or sets a condition about a person.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun referring to persons; it does not change for case. The final -i is not a case ending but a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting (elidable) alif.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'he took (for himself), adopted, or acquired' — to take something and make it one's own; from a reflexive pattern implying taking to oneself.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form VIII verb, third-person masculine singular ('he took'). Form VIII often carries a reflexive sense (taking for oneself). The final -a is the standard perfect ending, marking a completed act. The initial alif is a connecting hamza, sounded only at the start of an utterance.

4.meaning: His god / his deity — the object of worship that someone has taken for himself, referring to following one's desires as a god.
4.grammar: The noun ilāh (god, deity) from the root ʾ-l-h (to worship, to be a deity), in the accusative case (fatḥa) as the object of ittakhadha (took as). With third-person masculine singular possessive suffix -hu: his deity/god.
4.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — deity, god; the root of worship

5.meaning: His desire / his craving — the pull of one's lower self toward what it wants; whim, passion, or inclination, especially when it leads away from truth.
5.grammar: A noun ('desire, whim') with an attached third-person masculine singular possessive pronoun '-hu' ('his'), showing that the desire belongs to him. The word ends in a long final vowel (ā) and does not take a visible case mark, so its case is shown only by context.
5.root: ه-و-ي (h-w-y) — to incline, to fall; inclination, desire, whim

6.meaning: And Allah lets him go astray / and Allah leads him astray — referring to Allah sealing the misguidance of one who stubbornly refuses the truth.

parts.en: He led him astray / He allowed him to go astray

6.grammar: Conjunction waw + third-person masculine singular perfect verb from the root ḍ-l-l (to go astray), Form IV (aḍalla: to lead astray, to allow to go astray), with third-person masculine singular object suffix -hu. Subject is Allah.
6.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, be misguided; Form IV: to mislead

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

9.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
9.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'

10.meaning: And He sets a seal / and He placed a seal — Allah sealing the heart and faculties of the stubborn disbeliever as a consequence of their persistent rejection.
10.grammar: Conjunction waw + third-person masculine singular perfect verb from the root kh-t-m (to seal, stamp, close). Form I verb khatama. The subject is Allah (implied). The sealing is a metaphor for closing off the ability to perceive the truth.

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

12.meaning: His hearing — referring to the hearing of the disbeliever, which Allah seals so he can no longer benefit from truth.
12.grammar: The verbal noun samʿ (hearing) from the root s-m-ʿ (to hear), in the genitive case (kasra) as the object of the preposition ʿalā or in iḍāfa, with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix -hi.

13.meaning: And his heart — the seat of understanding, feeling, intention, and faith. Qalb denotes the inner core of a person (commonly 'heart' or 'mind'), the locus of thought and emotion. The word carries a connecting 'and' and the possessive 'his.'
13.grammar: A masculine noun with an attached possessive pronoun, preceded by 'and.' wa- means 'and.' The -i ending is genitive — the case that links the noun to a preceding noun or follows a preposition; the -hi form of 'his' is the variant used after an i-vowel.
13.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn, to overturn

14.meaning: 'And he made / appointed / rendered' — the connector 'and' joined to a past-tense verb meaning to make something into something, to fashion or appoint it. It can mean to create, to assign, or to cause a thing to become a certain way.
14.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a past-tense (perfect) verb. The bare verb with its final -a vowel denotes a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he made/did').
14.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

15.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
15.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

16.meaning: His vision / his sight — the physical or spiritual sight of the disbeliever, which is veiled and sealed.

parts.en: his vision / his sight (genitive with possessive)

16.grammar: Noun baṣar (vision, sight, eyesight) from the root b-ṣ-r (to see, perceive), in the genitive case (kasra) with third-person masculine singular possessive suffix -hi.
16.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, perceive, have insight

17.meaning: A veil / a cover — a covering placed over the sight of the disbeliever, preventing him from perceiving the truth.

parts.en: a veil / a covering / a film (accusative indefinite)

17.grammar: A noun in the accusative case (fatḥa + tanwīn, indefinite) from the root gh-sh-w/y (to cover, veil). Pattern fiʿāla. Refers to a covering placed over the eyes or the heart, preventing sight and understanding.

18.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
18.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

19.meaning: Will guide him — who then can guide this person whom Allah has let go astray and sealed? The rhetorical question implies: no one.

parts.en: will guide him / who guides him

19.grammar: Third-person masculine singular imperfect indicative verb from the root h-d-y (to guide), Form I: yahdī, with third-person masculine singular object suffix -hi (him). The indicative -ī ending is retained with the object pronoun.
19.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead to the right path

20.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
20.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

21.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
21.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
21.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

22.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
22.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

23.meaning: 'Then will you not…?' — a rhetorical opener combining 'then/so,' a question, and a negation, used to prompt reflection ('do you then not…?').
23.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb: the question marker 'a-' ('?'), the connector 'fa-' ('then/so'), and the negator 'lā' ('not'). Together they form a rhetorical question expecting agreement — 'will you then not…?' It has no case or tense ending of its own.

24.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) take heed, bear in mind, call to remembrance' — to reflect and let something sink in as a reminder.
24.grammar: A present-tense Form V verb (tafaʿʿala type, whose stem ta- is dropped by assimilation after the present-tense prefix). The ta- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' as the doers in the ordinary (indicative) present, describing ongoing or habitual action.
24.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

1.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: A standalone pronoun meaning 'she' or 'it' (feminine). Arabic has no neuter, so 'it' for a feminine noun is expressed with this word. Used independently for emphasis or to stand as the subject of a sentence.
3.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person feminine singular. It stands on its own (not attached to another word) and most often functions as the subject of a nominal sentence ('she/it is …'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

4.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
4.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

5.meaning: "Our life." The noun "life" — living existence, the state of being alive — with "our" attached.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the attached possessive "-nā" ("our"). The -u before the suffix marks the nominative case — the case a noun takes as the subject of a sentence or as the word that completes it.
5.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — to live; life

6.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
6.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
6.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

7.meaning: We die — the disbelievers claiming that death is the final end, denying resurrection.
7.grammar: First-person plural imperfect indicative verb from the root m-w-t (to die). Pattern: yamūtu → namūtu (we die). The -u ending is the indicative mood marker.

8.meaning: And we live — paired with 'we die,' the disbelievers claim life and death are merely natural processes with no divine purpose or resurrection.
8.grammar: Conjunction waw + first-person plural imperfect indicative verb from the root ḥ-y-y/ḥ-y-w (to live): naḥyā. The final alif (maqṣūra) represents the indicative -ī ending with a weak letter.
8.root: ح-ي-ي/و (ḥ-y-y) — to live, to be alive

9.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
9.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

10.meaning: Destroys us / causes us to perish — the disbelievers attribute their death and destruction to time (al-dahr) rather than to Allah.

parts.en: destroys us / causes us to perish

10.grammar: Third-person masculine singular imperfect indicative verb from the root h-l-k (to perish, be destroyed), Form IV: ahlaka (to destroy, cause to perish) → yuhliku, with first-person plural object suffix -nā. The subject is al-dahr (time) in the disbelievers' claim.
10.root: ه-ل-ك (h-l-k) — to perish, be destroyed; Form IV: to destroy

11.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
11.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

12.meaning: The time / al-dahr — the disbelievers' term for the passage of time, which they blame for death and decay, denying Allah's role as Creator and Judge.

parts.en: the time / the age / the passage of time (nominative definite)

12.grammar: Definite noun with the article al- (the), followed by the noun dahr (time, age, long period) from the root d-h-r. Nominative case (-u ending) as the subject of the verb yuhliku. Al-dahr here represents the materialist/fatalist belief of the disbelievers.

13.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
13.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

14.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
14.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

15.meaning: About that, with that, by that — bidhālika is the preposition bi- (with, by, about) plus the demonstrative pronoun dhālika (that — masculine singular distal).
15.grammar: Bi- is a preposition governing the demonstrative dhālika (which doesn't inflect for case; it is invariable). The phrase functions as an adverbial: 'about/concerning that thing'.
15.root: — (bi is a particle; dhā-lika is a demonstrative; no triliteral root)

16.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
16.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

17.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
17.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'

18.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
18.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

19.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
19.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

20.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
20.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

21.meaning: 'They think / are sure / expect' — to hold something as one's settled conviction or to reckon it likely; the verb spans from firm certainty to strong supposition.
21.grammar: The prefix 'ya-' marks a 3rd-person present-tense verb, and the '-ūna' ending makes the subject a masculine-inclusive plural 'they.' The '-ūna' is the indicative marker, signalling a plain factual or ongoing statement.
21.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to think, suppose, be convinced

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: It is being recited or read aloud — said of verses or scripture conveyed by voice, in an ongoing or repeated manner.

parts.en: recite/read aloud (passive stem, root letters t-l + long ā)

2.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) passive verb in the third person feminine singular ('it/she is recited'). The tu- prefix marks both the present tense and the passive voice ('is being …-ed'), so the doer is unnamed and the focus is on what undergoes the action. The stem -tlā keeps the second root consonant (t) and ends in a long ā written with ى, the shape a weak-final (defective) root takes when no further ending is attached.
2.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

3.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
3.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
3.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: Our signs / verses — 'āyāt' are tokens, proofs, and miraculous indications that point to a deeper truth, and also the verses of revelation; with 'Our' it refers to such signs ascribed to Allah.
4.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs, verses') with the attached possessive 'our' = -nā. The -u vowel before the pronoun marks the subject/naming case, the form a noun takes as the doer or topic of a sentence ('Our signs [are/do...]').
4.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token, miraculous indication

5.meaning: Clear, manifest, self-evident — the feminine plural of 'bayyin', describing things that are plainly evident and make matters distinct; an intensive adjective implying something that clarifies and is itself unmistakable.
5.grammar: A sound feminine plural adjective. The '-in' (nunation) ending marks it indefinite and in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case, so it agrees with an indefinite feminine plural noun it describes ('clear ___').
5.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct, evident; to make plain

6.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
6.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
6.root: — (particle; no root)

7.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

7.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

8.meaning: Their argument / their excuse — the false argument or pretext that the disbelievers could present on the Day of Judgment.

parts.en: their argument / their proof / their excuse (accusative with possessive)

8.grammar: Noun ḥujja (argument, proof, excuse) from the root ḥ-j-j (to argue, to make pilgrimage), in the accusative case (fatḥa) with third-person masculine plural possessive suffix -hum.
8.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — to argue, to refute; pilgrimage; proof

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
10.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

11.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

12.meaning: A command addressed to a group of males: 'come!' / 'bring (something)!' From a verb meaning to come, arrive, or bring something forth.
12.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending addresses a plural masculine group, directing them to perform the act: 'come' or 'bring.' The initial hamzat al-waṣl (i-) is a helping vowel that smooths pronunciation at the start.
12.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, or bring

13.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'fathers / forefathers / ancestors,' joined to 'our': 'our forefathers.' The bi- prefix links it to a preceding word (often after a verb of bringing or an oath/question).
13.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the possessive pronoun -nā ('our'), prefixed by bi-. The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, required because the noun follows the preposition bi-; the genitive typically marks a word that is governed by a preposition or linked to another noun.

14.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
14.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

15.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
15.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

16.meaning: The plural of 'ṣādiq': 'truthful ones', 'those who speak the truth', 'the sincere and reliable'. It describes people whose words and conduct match reality.
16.grammar: 'ṣādiq' is an active participle ('one who is truthful'). The '-īna' ending is a 'sound' masculine plural marker; the '-ī-' form (rather than '-ū-') signals that the noun is functioning as an object or is governed by a preposition/particle, while the '-na' completes the plural ('the truthful ones').
16.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, to speak truly

1.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: 'He gives life' or 'He brings to life' — a causative verb from the root meaning life: to make alive, to revive, to grant living existence to what was lifeless.
3.grammar: Present/future tense. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') in the causative (form IV) pattern; the imperfect without a jussive/subjunctive ending expresses ongoing or future action ('he gives / will give life'). The attached -kum is a plural object pronoun, 'you (all)'.

4.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
4.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

5.meaning: 'He causes (someone) to die' — a causative verb from the root meaning death: to bring about death, to make a living thing die. The causative form turns 'to die' into 'to put to death / to cause to die'.
5.grammar: Present/future tense. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') in the causative (form IV) pattern; the bare unending imperfect signals ongoing or future action ('he will / does cause to die'). The attached -kum is a plural object pronoun, 'you (all)'.
5.root: م-و-ت (m-w-t) — death, dying

6.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
6.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

7.meaning: He will gather you — Allah gathering all of humanity on the Day of Resurrection for judgment.

parts.en: He gathers you / He will gather you all

7.grammar: Third-person masculine singular imperfect indicative verb from the root j-m-ʿ (to gather, collect, assemble), Form I: yajmaʿu, with second-person masculine plural object suffix -kum. Subject is Allah (implied from context).
7.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — to gather, collect, assemble, unite

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
8.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

9.meaning: 'Day' — a span of time. It denotes a day or a definite point/period of time; it links to a following word to specify which day (e.g., 'the day of …').
9.grammar: A masculine noun. Its final -i vowel is the genitive case: it typically appears after a preposition or when the word is linked to a following noun in an 'of …' relationship (as in 'the day OF …').

10.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
10.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

11.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

12.meaning: Doubt, suspicion, disquieting uncertainty — the kind of wavering that unsettles the heart, stronger than a passing question. It names the state of not being at rest about whether something is true.
12.grammar: A masculine singular noun shown with an -a ending and no tanwin. This is the accusative (mansub) noun governed by the negating particle la — its ism — taking a bare form to express absolute negation, conveying that the whole category is ruled out ('there is no doubt whatsoever').

13.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
13.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

14.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
14.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

15.meaning: 'More' / 'greater (in number or amount)' — the comparative/superlative form built from 'much, many', meaning more numerous or more abundant.
15.grammar: A comparative adjective on the pattern afʿal ('more …'). The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is an object or otherwise governed; this pattern does not take nunation. It is typically completed by 'than …'.

16.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
16.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
16.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')
