17.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
17.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

18.meaning: They know / they have knowledge — an ongoing or habitual knowing by a group.
18.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the third person; plurality is supplied by the -ūna ending, which together with the prefix gives 'they'. The full -ūna ending also marks the ordinary indicative mood — a plain statement of present or ongoing action.

1.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and to Allah (belongs)' — expressing ownership or rightful belonging to Allah; the lām conveys possession or entitlement.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the prepositional phrase 'lillāhi'. This phrase is the preposition 'li-' ('to/for', here showing possession) prefixed to the name 'Allah'; when 'li-' attaches, the connecting hamza and the first lām of the definite article are elided in writing, leaving a single written lām for the preposition followed by the doubled (shadda-bearing) lām of the name. 'Allah' takes the -i (genitive) ending required after a preposition.

2.meaning: Kingdom, dominion, sovereign rule — full ownership and authority over a realm; the right and power to command and dispose.
2.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u marks the nominative case, used when the noun is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('the dominion is …'). The absence of nunation here points to its being made definite by a following possessor in a genitive link.
2.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule; kingship, dominion

3.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

4.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
4.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

5.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
5.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.
5.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, time

6.meaning: You stand / you rise — second-person masculine singular present of 'to stand up or rise'; used for standing in prayer or for arising at night for worship.

parts.en: you stand / rise (Form I muḍāriʿ 2nd masculine singular)

6.grammar: Form I muḍāriʿ second-person masculine singular (ta- prefix, -u indicative). The root q-w-m conveys rising, standing, and establishing oneself — including the standing of prayer.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; establishment

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hour' — a moment or short span of time. In its weighty sense it names the Last Hour, the appointed time of resurrection and final reckoning. Built with the definite article 'the.'
7.grammar: A definite noun (the 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 's,' doubling it). The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a verb or sentence.
7.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — relating to an hour, a moment, or a span of time

8.meaning: On that day / that day — pointing back to a particular past day already in view; 'a day, at that time.'
8.grammar: A time-word ('day') joined to 'idhin' ('at that time'), together meaning 'on that day.' The '-in' ('tanwīn') compensates for an understood clause ('the day when…'). The form functions adverbially, locating an event at a specific past moment.

9.meaning: Will lose / they will be losers — those who rejected the truth will suffer loss on the Day of Judgment.
9.grammar: Third-person masculine singular (or plural with different reading) imperfect indicative verb from the root kh-s-r (to lose, suffer loss, incur a loss). The -u ending marks the indicative mood.
9.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — to lose, incur loss, be in deficit

10.meaning: Those who pursue falsehood / the perpetrators of vanity — people who deal in what is false, baseless, or futile, or who try to nullify the truth.
10.grammar: A definite active participle (the doer) from the causative pattern, naming those who engage in falsehood or seek to invalidate truth. The '-ūna' ending marks the masculine plural in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
10.root: ب-ط-ل (b-ṭ-l) — falsehood, vanity, to be null/void

1.meaning: 'And you see / you will see / you behold' — the connector 'and' with a present-tense verb of seeing, perceiving with the eyes, or coming to realize.
1.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') plus a present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix signals a second-person singular subject ('you'). Because the root ends in a weak letter, the verb closes in a long -ā rather than a short vowel; it reads as a plain statement, 'you see.'
1.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, behold, consider

2.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
2.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

3.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
3.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.

4.meaning: Kneeling / on their knees — describing each nation prostrated or kneeling before Allah on the Day of Judgment, awaiting their reckoning.
4.grammar: Active participle (ism fāʿil) of the verb jathā (to kneel, crouch), feminine form jāthiya, in the accusative case (fatḥa + tanwīn, indefinite) as a ḥāl (circumstantial qualifier). Describes the posture of every nation awaiting judgment.

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'all, every, each, the whole of.' It expresses totality — when joined to a following noun it means 'every (one)' or 'the entirety of' that thing.
5.grammar: A noun of totality with the final -u ending (nominative). The -u typically marks it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It normally attaches to a following noun to mean 'every / all of' it.
5.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, wholeness, comprehensiveness

6.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
6.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.
6.root: ء-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — community, way, intent

7.meaning: Will be called / they will be summoned — every nation or people being called to their record on the Day of Judgment.

parts.en: it/they will be called / summoned (passive imperfect, feminine singular)

7.grammar: Third-person feminine singular imperfect passive verb from the root d-ʿ-w (to call, summon, invite), Form I passive: tudʿā (she/it will be called). The feminine agrees with umma (nation) or related feminine referent.
7.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, pray

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
8.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

9.meaning: Its record / its book — the book or record of a nation's deeds that will be presented before it on the Day of Judgment.

parts.en: its record / its book (accusative with feminine possessive)

9.grammar: Noun kitāb (book, record, scripture) in the accusative case (fatḥa) with third-person feminine singular possessive suffix -hā, referring back to umma (nation, feminine).

10.meaning: The day / today: a 'day' as a unit of time; with the article it points to the present day, 'this day' or 'today', the time at hand.
10.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative ending; for a time-word this commonly functions adverbially, marking 'when' something happens (e.g. 'on the day', 'today').

11.meaning: 'You are recompensed / repaid' — a passive verb meaning a group is given back what their deeds deserve, whether reward or penalty. The doer (the One who repays) is understood, not named.
11.grammar: A present/imperfect passive verb (form I). The tu- prefix with passive vowelling plus the -una ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject being acted upon ('you [all] are repaid'). The -una (not -u) shows the indicative mood, used for plain factual statements.
11.root: ج-ز-ى (j-z-y) — recompense, requital, repaying in kind

12.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

13.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
13.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

14.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
14.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
1.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

2.meaning: Our Record / Our Book — the comprehensive divine record kept by Allah containing the deeds of all people.

parts.en: Our Record / Our Book (nominative with first person plural possessive)

2.grammar: Noun kitāb (book, record) in the nominative case (-u ending) with first-person plural possessive suffix -nā (Our), referring to the divine book kept by Allah containing the record of all deeds.
2.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write, book, scripture, record

3.meaning: Speaks / declares — the divine record will speak truthfully about all that people did, with complete accuracy.

parts.en: it speaks / it declares / it articulates (indicative)

3.grammar: Third-person masculine singular imperfect indicative verb from the root n-ṭ-q (to speak, articulate, declare). The -u ending marks the indicative mood. The subject is kitāb (the Record).

4.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
4.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

5.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
5.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
5.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

6.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
6.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

7.meaning: 'We were' — the past tense of the verb 'to be,' establishing a past state or condition for a group including the speaker. It is the basic verb of existence and of 'being something.'
7.grammar: The past tense of 'to be' in the first-person plural ('we were'). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'); its nūn is written with a shadda (نَّ) because it merges with the final nūn of the verb stem kun-, and the alif spells the long -ā. A hollow verb, its middle weak letter drops in this form. It sets up a past state, and what follows describes how 'we' were.
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, existence

8.meaning: We transcribe / We record — Allah declaring that His angels record and copy down all that people do.

parts.en: We transcribe / We copy / We record (indicative, Form X)

8.grammar: First-person plural imperfect indicative verb from the root n-s-kh (to copy, transcribe, abrogate), Form X (istafʿala): istansikha, meaning 'to copy out, to transcribe.' The Form X adds a sense of careful, deliberate recording. The -u ending marks indicative mood.
8.root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh) — to copy, transcribe, abrogate, supersede

9.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

10.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
10.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
10.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

11.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
11.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: 'Then as for …' A connective opening that introduces and singles out a topic for comment, often paired later with a response. The fa- means 'then/so,' and 'ammā' sets up 'as for (such-and-such)…' to highlight one case among others.
1.grammar: A connector fa- ('then, so') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā introduces a subject for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that gives the comment about it. Neither part takes case endings.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
4.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

5.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
5.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
5.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

6.meaning: Will admit them / He will cause them to enter — Allah admitting the righteous believers into Paradise.

parts.en: so He will admit them / He will cause them to enter (Form IV with object)

6.grammar: Conjunction fa (so/then) + third-person masculine singular imperfect indicative verb from the root d-kh-l (to enter), Form IV (adkhala: to admit, cause to enter) → yudkhilu, with third-person masculine plural object suffix -hum. Subject is Allah.
6.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter; Form IV: to admit, cause to enter

7.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Nurturer who owns, provides, and brings to maturity) joined to the pronoun 'their'.
7.grammar: A noun with a possessive pronoun. The -u vowel before -hum is the nominative ending, typically marking the word as the subject/doer. The suffix -hum means 'their', referring to a masculine plural group.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master, to nurture and sustain

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: His mercy — His compassion, tenderness, and loving-kindness that actively bestows good and relief. "Raḥmah" is mercy as an outpouring of care, here possessed by Him.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun with an attached possessive "His." The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun or preposition ("… of …"). The pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows that -i vowel.

10.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
10.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

11.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
11.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

12.meaning: 'The success' / 'the triumph' — attainment of what is sought and safety from what is feared; winning, salvation, the great achievement. With the article it is 'the (true) success'.
12.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -u ending is the nominative case, marking it as a subject or as the thing identified (e.g. 'that IS the success').
12.root: ف-و-ز (f-w-z) — to win, triumph, attain salvation

13.meaning: Clear, plain, manifest; that which makes things evident — both 'clearly apparent in itself' and 'making the truth clear to others'.
13.grammar: An active participle, 'the one that makes clear / the manifest', from a causative (form-IV) pattern, carried by the definite article al- ('the'). The final -u ending is the nominative case, the form used when the word serves as a subject or as a descriptor of such a word.

1.meaning: 'And as for …' A connective that introduces and sets apart a new topic for separate comment, usually anticipating a matching response clause. The 'and' joins it on; 'ammā' means 'as for (such-and-such)…'
1.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā singles out a topic for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that supplies the comment. Neither part takes case endings.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: Disbelieved — those who rejected faith and denied the truth of Allah's signs and messengers.

parts.en: they disbelieved / they rejected faith (perfect plural)

3.grammar: Third-person masculine plural perfect verb from the root k-f-r (to disbelieve, reject, cover up the truth). Pattern: kafara → kafarū (plural). The alif after waw is orthographic, not pronounced.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to disbelieve, reject, cover up (truth/blessings)

4.meaning: "so have they then not…?" — a clustered opener combining 'so/then' with a questioning 'have they not?'; it poses a rebuking or prompting question about something that has not yet happened, urging reflection.
4.grammar: Three particles fused together: the questioning a- ('?'), the connective fa- ('so/then'), and lam, which negates and pushes a following present-tense verb into the meaning 'has/did not (do)'. Together they introduce a pointed rhetorical question about a past or completed matter.

5.meaning: A short (jussive) form of the verb 'to be / to become', meaning 'be' or 'does not become / is not'. It expresses being, existing, or coming to be in a clipped form that typically follows a particle such as a negator or a command.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person masculine singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, the form used after negative particles ('did not / was not') or as a command or prohibition.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

6.meaning: My signs / My verses — clear tokens, proofs, or revealed verses that point to a truth, here belonging to the speaker ('My').
6.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun ('signs') with the attached possessive -ī meaning 'my'. The plural is built with the -āt ending; the long -ī suffix marks first-person singular ownership.
6.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

7.meaning: It is being recited or read aloud — said of verses or scripture conveyed by voice, in an ongoing or repeated manner.

parts.en: recite/read aloud (passive stem, root letters t-l + long ā)

7.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) passive verb in the third person feminine singular ('it/she is recited'). The tu- prefix marks both the present tense and the passive voice ('is being …-ed'), so the doer is unnamed and the focus is on what undergoes the action. The stem -tlā keeps the second root consonant (t) and ends in a long ā written with ى, the shape a weak-final (defective) root takes when no further ending is attached.
7.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

8.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
8.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

9.meaning: But you were proud / you acted arrogantly — the disbelievers were told to submit but refused out of arrogance.

parts.en: you were proud / you acted arrogantly (Form X, perfect plural)

9.grammar: Conjunction fa + second-person masculine plural perfect verb from the root k-b-r (to be great), Form X (istakbara: to consider oneself great, to be arrogant, to refuse with pride). The Form X indicates a reflexive sense of self-aggrandizement.
9.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great, large; Form X: to act arrogantly, deem oneself great

10.meaning: And you (plural) were — reporting a past state or ongoing condition of a group of people.
10.grammar: The connector 'and' attached to the past tense of the verb 'to be'. The ending -tum marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the subject. This verb sets up a description of a state in the past ('you all were …'), and it typically introduces the condition or situation that followed.
10.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come into being

11.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
11.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
11.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

12.meaning: Wrongdoers / criminals / guilty ones — those who commit grave sins and crimes, who deliberately cut themselves off from right and break with what is good.
12.grammar: An active participle of the form IV pattern (ajrama, 'to commit a crime'), sound masculine plural ('wrongdoers'). The -īna ending is the plural form used when the noun is an object or follows a preposition (the oblique/genitive-accusative case), as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
12.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime, sin, cut off

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: 'It was said' — speech was uttered or a statement was made. The passive form: the saying is reported without naming who spoke.

parts.en: was said (passive verb stem of the root q-w-l)
he/it (default short vowel of the 3rd masc. sg. past)

2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice (pattern qīla) from the hollow root ق-و-ل. The passive is formed by internal vowel change: the middle radical (wāw) is replaced by a long 'ī', which marks the verb as passive (the doer is left unnamed). The lām is the third root letter, not an ending; the final -a is simply the default short vowel of the third-person masculine singular past, here used impersonally as 'it was said'.

3.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
3.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

4.meaning: 'a promise / pledge' — a binding assurance of something to come; here as a noun naming the thing pledged or the act of pledging.
4.grammar: A verbal noun with the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as a direct object or as an emphatic inner object reinforcing a verb of the same meaning ('a promise [truly promised]'). It names the act/content of promising.
4.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, give an assurance

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: 'Truth, reality, a rightful due' — that which is firmly real, correct, and established; also a right or claim that is owed. As a descriptor it means 'true, real, well-founded.'
6.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -un ending (nominative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) is the form a noun takes as the subject or as the completing word of a statement ('is true/real').
6.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, what is due

7.meaning: And the Hour — referring to the Day of Judgment, the final Hour when all creation will be brought to account.

parts.en: the Hour (nominative definite) — the Day of Judgment

7.grammar: Conjunction waw + definite noun al-sāʿa (the Hour) from the root s-w-ʿ (or ṣ-w-ʿ — the root for hour/moment), in the nominative case (-u ending). Al-Sāʿa is a Quranic term specifically for the Day of Resurrection and Judgment.
7.root: س-و-ع / س-ع-ي (s-w-ʿ) — hour, moment; the Hour of Judgment

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: Doubt, suspicion, disquieting uncertainty — the kind of wavering that unsettles the heart, stronger than a passing question. It names the state of not being at rest about whether something is true.
9.grammar: A masculine singular noun shown with an -a ending and no tanwin. This is the accusative (mansub) noun governed by the negating particle la — its ism — taking a bare form to express absolute negation, conveying that the whole category is ruled out ('there is no doubt whatsoever').

10.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
10.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

11.meaning: 'You (plural) said' — to say, speak, or utter. The verb covers any act of stating or declaring something in words.
11.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix -tum marks the masculine plural 'you (all)' as the doers of a completed action — it signals both the past tense and that the speakers being addressed are a group. (This is a hollow verb: its middle root letter is a wāw, which surfaces as a long ā in the base form qāla but reduces to a short u, giving qul-, before a consonant-initial suffix like -tum.)
11.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

12.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
12.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

13.meaning: We know — the disbelievers denying knowledge of the Hour, or believers affirming that only Allah knows it.

parts.en: we know / we are aware (indicative, first person plural)

13.grammar: First-person plural imperfect indicative verb from the root d-r-y (to know, be aware of, understand). The final yāʾ is the weak root letter. Often used in negative constructions: mā nadrī (we do not know).
13.root: د-ر-ي (d-r-y) — to know, be aware of, understand

14.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
14.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

15.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hour' — a moment or short span of time. In its weighty sense it names the Last Hour, the appointed time of resurrection and final reckoning. Built with the definite article 'the.'
15.grammar: A definite noun (the 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 's,' doubling it). The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a verb or sentence.
15.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — relating to an hour, a moment, or a span of time

16.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
16.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

17.meaning: We think / we suppose — used to express conjecture or doubt, often about the Hour or resurrection.

parts.en: we think / we suppose / we conjecture (indicative, first person plural)

17.grammar: First-person plural imperfect indicative verb from the root ẓ-n-n (to think, suppose, conjecture), with doubled final letter (geminated nūn). The -u ending marks the indicative mood. Ẓann typically indicates conjecture rather than certainty.
17.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to think, suppose, conjecture, suspect

18.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
18.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

19.meaning: 'Conjecture, assumption, supposition' — ẓann is a thought or opinion held without certain knowledge: a guess, surmise, or presumption that may be strong but falls short of sure knowledge. The base root spans suspicion, opinion, and supposition.
19.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a conjecture'). The -an ending (written with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative, often marking the direct object of a verb, an adverbial sense ('by way of conjecture'), or what is specified after certain words.
19.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to suppose, conjecture, think without certainty

20.meaning: A compound: the connective 'and' joined to the particle mā. The particle mā is highly versatile — it can mean 'what / whatever' (introducing an indirect question or a relative clause, 'that which'), or it can function as a negation ('not'). Context determines which sense applies; the core idea is an open, unspecified 'what(ever)' or a flat denial.
20.grammar: Two indeclinable particles, so there is no case ending to mark. The wa- prefix is the simple connective 'and', linking what follows to what precedes. Mā itself does not change form: it serves either as an interrogative/relative ('what, that which') or as a negating word ('not').

21.meaning: 'We' — the standalone pronoun for a speaker including others (or a single speaker of majesty). It stands alone to name or emphasize the subject 'we'.
21.grammar: A detached (standalone) personal pronoun, first-person plural, 'we'. Such independent pronouns are used to state or emphasize the subject, often highlighting 'we' as the ones who do or are something.

22.meaning: Convinced / certain — the disbelievers who are certain (wrongly) that the Hour will not come, or believers who are certain it will.

parts.en: convinced / certain ones (active participle, Form X, accusative/genitive plural)

22.grammar: Preposition bi (with/by) + active participle of Form X istayqana (to be fully certain, to be convinced), masculine plural in the genitive/accusative case (marked by the -īna ending instead of -ūna). Form X of y-q-n (certainty, sure knowledge).
22.root: ي-ق-ن (y-q-n) — certainty, sure knowledge; Form X: to be fully convinced/certain

1.meaning: And (will) appear — wabadā means 'and it appeared', 'and it became manifest', describing the sudden manifestation of evil deeds and their consequences on Judgment Day.

parts.en: it appeared, it became manifest, it was exposed

1.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction. Badā is Form I perfect (third masculine singular) from root b-d-w/b-d-y, meaning to appear, to become manifest, to be revealed. The alif maqṣūra marks the weak root. Context: 'And the evil of what they did appeared to them' — on Judgment Day, their evil deeds will be openly exposed.
1.root: ب-د-و/ي (b-d-w/y) — to appear, to become visible, to be manifest

2.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

3.meaning: Evil deeds / evil consequences — bad actions and the harmful results they bring; misdeeds, offenses, and the afflictions that issue from them. The plural of a word denoting a bad or harmful thing.
3.grammar: A feminine plural noun. The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically identifies the noun as the subject (the doer or topic) of its clause. Being grammatically incomplete on its own, it commonly stands in a possessive link with a following noun ('the evil deeds of …').
3.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil; to harm

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: They did / they worked — to perform a deed or action, to do work. The base word covers purposeful action and labor.
5.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending marks 'they' (a group of males) as the doers (the silent alif after it is a spelling convention).
5.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, act, work, perform a deed

6.meaning: And it closed in / encompassed — to surround completely and descend upon, especially of a punishment or consequence that envelops people and leaves no escape.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb (a hollow root, whose middle letter appears as the long 'ā'). It is third-person masculine singular ('he/it did') and complete in the past; it characteristically governs a following 'with/upon' to name those whom the encirclement befalls. The prefixed wa- simply means 'and.'
6.root: ح-ي-ق (ḥ-y-q) — to surround, beset, encompass

7.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
7.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

8.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
8.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

9.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
9.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

10.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
10.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

11.meaning: To mock, ridicule, scoff at, or deride — to treat something with derision and make light of it. The form conveys a sustained or repeated attitude of scornful jesting.
11.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb of the Form X pattern (the 'sta-' element, here seeking/intensifying the sense of mockery). The 'ya-…-ūna' frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject — 'they' do or are doing the action. The '-ūna' ending signals the plural 'they' and that the verb is in its full (indicative) form, real and ongoing.

1.meaning: And it was said — a statement was uttered or a command was given (by an unnamed speaker).
1.grammar: A past-tense passive verb. The internal vowel pattern (qīla, with 'ī') marks it as passive — the doer is unspecified, so it means 'it was said' rather than 'he said.' The final '-a' is the standard ending of a third-person masculine singular past verb.

2.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'the day,' very often used to mean 'today' or 'this day.' With the definite article it points to the present day as a defined, known span of time, and by extension can denote 'now' or 'the present moment.'
2.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending; on a noun of time it commonly marks it as an adverb answering 'when?' — fixing the action to that period ('on the day', 'today').
2.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

3.meaning: We forget you / We shall neglect you — on the Day of Judgment Allah will say to the disbelievers: just as you forgot Us, We shall forget you (i.e., leave you to your punishment).

parts.en: We forget you / We neglect you (imperfect indicative with object)

3.grammar: First-person plural imperfect indicative verb from the root n-s-y (to forget, neglect), with second-person masculine plural object suffix -kum. The alif maqṣūra (ā) at the end is the indicator of the weak root. 'We forget you' here means abandonment to punishment.

4.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
4.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) forgot' or 'you neglected' — from the root for forgetting, which spans both losing something from memory and deliberately disregarding or abandoning it.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The '-tum' ending marks the doer as 'you all' (a group, masculine). The root sense covers both genuine forgetting and willful neglect or disregard.
5.root: ن-س-ي (n-s-y) — to forget; to neglect/abandon

6.meaning: Meeting, encounter, or coming-face-to-face — the event of two parties meeting, often used of the encounter with one's Lord or an appointed reckoning.
6.grammar: A verbal noun (the act of meeting) on the 'fiʿāl' pattern. The final -a is the accusative case ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case.
6.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, come upon

7.meaning: Your day — a particular day belonging to or appointed for a group; 'day' here often points to a momentous appointed Day.
7.grammar: A noun 'day' with the genitive case ending -i (linking it to a preceding noun in an 'of' sense or following a preposition), plus the possessive -kum, 'your' (addressed to a group).
7.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — a day, a span of time

8.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
8.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

9.meaning: And your abode / and your dwelling — the final dwelling place of the disbelievers, which is the Fire.

parts.en: your abode / your dwelling / your refuge (nominative with possessive)

9.grammar: Conjunction waw + noun maʾwā (abode, dwelling, refuge, place of shelter) from the root ʾ-w-y (to take shelter, to lodge), with second-person masculine plural possessive suffix -kum (and the connector vowel -u before the next word). Nominative or as predicate.
9.root: أ-و-ي (ʾ-w-y) — to take shelter, lodge, give refuge; abode

10.meaning: The Fire — a definite noun for fire; frequently the term for the blazing punishment of the Hereafter (Hell).
10.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', heard as 'an-nār'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

12.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
12.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

13.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
13.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

14.meaning: Helpers / supporters: those who give aid, support, and victory to another, standing by them against an adversary; the plural of 'helper'.
14.grammar: A masculine plural active participle — a 'doer' word meaning 'ones who help'. The sound plural ending -īna marks more than two; this -īna form (rather than -ūna) is the case used for objects of verbs and after prepositions or in possession (the accusative/genitive).
14.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to give victory/support

1.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
1.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

2.meaning: Because you / in that you — explaining the reason for the punishment: it is because of what the disbelievers themselves chose to do.
2.grammar: Preposition bi (used here causally: 'because of') + conjunction anna (that, introducing a noun clause) + second-person masculine plural subject suffix -kum (with connecting vowel -u). Bi-anna + clause = 'because you...'

3.meaning: Took / adopted — the disbelievers took the revelations of Allah as a mockery, or adopted false objects of worship.

parts.en: you took / you adopted (Form VIII, perfect, second person plural)

3.grammar: Second-person masculine plural perfect verb from the root ʾ-kh-dh (to take), Form VIII (iftaʿala): ittakhadha (to take for oneself, adopt, treat as). The assimilation of the initial hamza and the taʾ of Form VIII gives ittakhadha.

4.meaning: Signs, tokens, or evident proofs; also used for the discrete verses of revelation. An āya is a marker that points beyond itself to a deeper truth or to its Author.
4.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs/verses'). The sound-feminine plural takes -i in both the genitive and accusative; the -i ending here links it to a following noun ('… of …') or marks it as the object of a verb or preposition.

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: Mockery, ridicule, a laughing-stock — the act of deriding, or an object treated as a joke. Huzuw is scornful jesting that belittles.
6.grammar: An indefinite verbal noun in the accusative ('an' written with tanwīn on a final alif). The accusative here is typical for the object of a verb or for stating what something is taken/treated 'as'. 'Indefinite' means 'mockery / a mockery' rather than 'the mockery'.
6.root: ه-ز-و (h-z-w) — to mock, ridicule, scoff at; a wāw-final variant of the related root ه-ز-أ (h-z-ʾ), this written form ending in wāw

7.meaning: And deceived you — the worldly life deceived the disbelievers, causing them to neglect the Hereafter.

parts.en: it deceived you / it deluded you (perfect, feminine subject with object)

7.grammar: Conjunction waw + third-person feminine singular perfect verb from the root gh-r-r (to deceive, delude), with second-person masculine plural object suffix -kum (with connecting vowel -u). The feminine verb agrees with al-ḥayāt al-dunyā (the worldly life, feminine) as subject.

8.meaning: 'The life' — earthly existence, the span of living in this world. The word denotes life as the state of being alive, vitality, and the worldly life as a whole.
8.grammar: 'al-' is the definite article 'the'. The final '-u' is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing or being something), or as the predicate naming what something is.

9.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
9.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
9.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

10.meaning: So / then — the day; a connective particle joined to the noun 'the day.' It links to what precedes (drawing a consequence or sequence, 'so / then') and names the day.
10.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connector meaning 'so / then,' marking a result or sequence. al- is 'the.' The final -a is the accusative case, which often marks a direct object or, with time-words like 'day,' an adverbial sense ('on the day').

11.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

12.meaning: They will be brought forth / they will be taken out — referring to people being brought out of the Fire or from their state, for punishment or reckoning.

parts.en: they will be brought out / they will be expelled (passive indicative plural)

12.grammar: Third-person masculine plural imperfect passive indicative verb from the root kh-r-j (to go out, exit), Form IV passive: ukhrija → yukhraju (they are brought out), with plural marker -ūna.
12.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to exit, go out; Form IV: to bring out, expel

13.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
13.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

14.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

15.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
15.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

16.meaning: They are asked to seek favor / given a chance to make amends; the passive of a verb meaning to be allowed to appease, return to good standing, or have one's plea for grace accepted. The root sense is reconciliation and seeking to please after a fault.
16.grammar: A present-tense passive verb (Form X) with the yu- prefix and -ūna ending marking a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood. The vowel pattern marks it as passive ('they are asked / made to seek favor').
16.root: ع-ت-ب (ʿ-t-b) — reproach, reconciliation, to seek favor

1.meaning: Then belonging to Allah; so it is Allah's. The phrase asserts that something pertains or belongs exclusively to Allah, introduced by a connective 'then/so'.
1.grammar: A connective 'fa-' ('then/so') plus the preposition 'li-' ('to/for/belonging to') attached to the name Allah. The '-i' ending on the name is genitive, the case required after a preposition; the combination expresses ownership or entitlement: '(it is) for/belonging to Allah'.

2.meaning: The praise — all commendation, thanks, and laudation. With the article it conveys praise as a whole, in its entirety, belonging by right to the one praised.
2.grammar: A verbal noun with the definite article 'al-'. The '-u' ending is nominative, marking it as the subject/topic of a sentence; with the article it carries the sense of 'all praise' as an entire, comprehensive category.

3.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
3.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

4.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

5.meaning: And (the) Lord — referring to Allah as the Lord of the heavens and earth, appearing in an oath or declaration.
5.grammar: Conjunction/oath waw + rabb (Lord, Sustainer) in the genitive case (kasra) as the first term of an iḍāfa. Rabb is from the root r-b-b (to nurture, sustain, be Lord). Here it introduces an oath: 'By the Lord of...'
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, be Lord of

6.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
6.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
6.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

7.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
7.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

8.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
8.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
8.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: 'And for Him / and to Him belongs' — the preposition 'for/to' expressing belonging or possession, joined with the pronoun 'Him.' It conveys that something belongs or is due to Him.
1.grammar: A small phrase: the connector 'and' plus the preposition la- ('for, to, belonging to') with the attached pronoun -hu ('Him'). The construction 'la- + pronoun' expresses possession or entitlement — 'and to Him belongs …' / 'and for Him is …'

2.meaning: Greatness, grandeur, supremacy — loftiness and pride of rank; the quality of standing above all others in majesty and dominion. It can name both true divine grandeur and the haughty self-exaltation of the proud.
2.grammar: An abstract noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The '-u' ending is nominative — the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being affirmed ('the grandeur is …').

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

5.meaning: And the earth — paired with 'the heavens,' completing the oath 'By the Lord of the heavens and the earth.'
5.grammar: Conjunction waw + definite noun al-arḍ (the earth) in the genitive case (kasra) as the second term of an iḍāfa after rabb (Lord of...). Al-arḍ is from the root ʾ-r-ḍ.
5.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — the earth, the ground, the land

6.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
6.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

7.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
7.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

8.meaning: "the All-Wise" — one full of wisdom, who judges and orders everything with perfect, sound judgement; as a divine name 'al-Ḥakīm' denotes the One whose every act and decree is supremely wise.
8.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, abiding quality ('ever-wise'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes as the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description.
8.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, govern; wisdom
